english: to be lucky / to get lucky (colloquial)
situation_en: Something went well by pure luck — you caught the delayed train, found the last free table, passed by one point.

example_sentences.de: Da hast du echt Schwein gehabt — der Zug hatte zum Glück Verspätung!
example_sentences.en: You really got lucky there — luckily the train was delayed!

example_sentences.de: Wir haben Schwein gehabt: Das waren die letzten zwei Tickets.
example_sentences.en: We got lucky: those were the last two tickets.

notes: Almost always in the Perfekt: Schwein gehabt! The pig is a German good-luck symbol (das Glücksschwein) — marzipan pigs are given as New Year presents.
related: Glück haben (neutral register), das Glücksschwein, Pech haben (opposite: to be unlucky)

situation_en: Someone is unsure what to do and you offer your opinion on what they should do.

example_sentences.de: Meine Oma gibt mir immer gute Ratschläge.
example_sentences.en: My grandma always gives me good advice.

example_sentences.de: Er gibt gern Ratschläge, ohne gefragt zu werden.
example_sentences.en: He likes giving advice without being asked.

notes: Fixed verb: geben (not machen!). Singular: einen Ratschlag / einen Rat geben. Ask for advice: jemanden um Rat fragen.
related: der Ratschlag (noun), um Rat fragen, der Tipp

english: please stay objective / stick to the facts
situation_en: A discussion is getting emotional or personal and you want to bring it back to the facts.

example_sentences.de: Die Diskussion wurde laut. „Bitte sachlich bleiben!“, sagte die Moderatorin.
example_sentences.en: The discussion got loud. "Please stay objective!", said the moderator.

example_sentences.de: Bleiben wir sachlich: Was sind die Fakten?
example_sentences.en: Let's stick to the facts: what are the facts?

notes: sachlich comes from die Sache (the matter). Core vocabulary for meetings, debates and online discussions. Opposite: persönlich/emotional werden.
related: sachlich (objective), die Sachlichkeit, zur Sache kommen (to get to the point)

english: anyway / be that as it may
situation_en: You want to close a topic, move on, or signal that the details don't matter right now.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer — wir müssen jetzt eine Entscheidung treffen.
example_sentences.en: Anyway — we have to make a decision now.

example_sentences.de: Wie auch immer, das Ergebnis bleibt gleich.
example_sentences.en: Be that as it may, the result stays the same.

notes: Discourse marker to change or close a topic — makes conversation flow naturally. Family: was auch immer (whatever), wo auch immer (wherever), wie dem auch sei (formal).
related: jedenfalls (in any case), egal (doesn't matter), wie dem auch sei

situation_en: You and someone else just made an arrangement or deal and you seal it.
notes: Partizip II of abmachen (to arrange/agree on — see Verbs). Used alone as a one-word answer to seal an agreement, like shaking hands verbally.

situation_en: Someone proposes something and you formally give your OK — or you ask someone for theirs.

example_sentences.de: Bist du mit dem Plan einverstanden?
example_sentences.en: Do you agree with the plan?

notes: Pattern: einverstanden sein mit + Dativ. As a standalone answer it is slightly more formal than Abgemacht. Noun: das Einverständnis (consent).

english: as much / as little / as often as possible
situation_en: You want to express 'to the maximum degree that is possible' without the long so-…-wie-möglich construction.

example_sentences.de: Trink möglichst viel Wasser — das ist gesund.
example_sentences.en: Drink as much water as possible — it's healthy.

example_sentences.de: Ich versuche, möglichst oft zu Fuß zu gehen.
example_sentences.en: I try to walk as often as possible.

notes: möglichst + adjective/adverb compresses 'so X wie möglich': möglichst schnell = so schnell wie möglich. Extremely common in instructions and advice.
related: so … wie möglich, möglich (possible), die Möglichkeit

english: to get confused / to get mixed up
situation_en: Too many names, numbers or similar words — and your head loses track.

example_sentences.de: Bei den vielen Namen komme ich durcheinander.
example_sentences.en: With all these names I get confused.

example_sentences.de: Ich bin mit den Terminen völlig durcheinander gekommen.
example_sentences.en: I got the appointments completely mixed up.

notes: durcheinander = mixed up, in disarray. Related: das Durcheinander (chaos/mess), etwas durcheinanderbringen (to mix things up). Perfekt with sein: Ich bin durcheinander gekommen.
related: das Durcheinander, durcheinanderbringen, verwechseln (to confuse two things)
